newsitem.title: USA: ING Barings cuts Argentina, Colombia in portfolio.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings cuts Argentina, Colombia in portfolio.

text.p: ING Barings cut its ratings for Argentina and Colombia Thursday to underweight from overweight in its model portfolio of Latin American stocks.

"Both markets have very limited expected year-end upside and investors should sell Argentina" after the U.S. central bank left interest rates unchanged and with a rally in industrial production, wrote Tim Love, head of Latin American research and strategy.

Colombia's strong stock market performance so far this year "is unlikely to continue due to weak economic growth, low expected EPS (earnings per share) growth for 1998 and increasing political and fiscal risk."
Love extended ING Barings' already strong overweight position in Brazil, raising the year-end target for the Ibovespa to 13,161 from 12,639.
Brazil "continues to reap bottom-up benefits from privatization," he said.
He raised Chile to neutral from underweight, saying, "Chile's prospective upside is now favorable compared to Argentina.
